title: Frontend crams the four things that identify a means of transport into one semicolon-separated sentence; Design release 1 sets them out as a bulleted list

finding.frontend: The hint under "Transport identification" is one sentence three lines long: "To identify the means of transport, enter (one of the following): flight number; train number; road vehicle registration number; vessel name (for ferries, also the road vehicle registration number)" (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/transport/copy/copy.en.js:26, rendered as a plain hint at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/transport/port-of-entry/port-of-entry.njk:41-48). The four alternatives are separated only by semicolons, and the last one carries its own parenthesis, so a reader has to parse punctuation to see that there are four choices and to see where the fourth one ends.
finding.prototype: The same hint is a lead-in sentence, "To identify the means of transport, enter (one of the following):", followed by a bulleted list of four items — flight number, train number, road vehicle registration number, and vessel name (for ferries, also the road vehicle registration number) (app/views/arrival-details.html:128). Each alternative sits on its own line and the number of choices is visible without reading.
finding.difference: Split the transport identification hint into a lead-in sentence and a four-item bulleted list, keeping the wording of the items exactly as it is. The frontend's hint is currently a single string in copy, so the copy entry has to become a lead sentence plus a list of items and the template has to render the list rather than pass a bare string to the hint's text.
finding.falsifiedBy: Finding a bulleted list inside the frontend's transport identification hint in the captured rendered DOM of fe-arrival-details.
